Mr. Priyank Rathi, Govt. Advocate for the State.

Mr. Cartis Colins, learned counsel for the
Respondent No. 2.

Learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that the present case arises out of a matrimonial dispute between the petitioner (wife) and the complainant (husband), whose marriage was solemnized on 12.04.2012 at Chennai with the consent of both families, and their relationship remained cordial initially.

The complainant later alleged that during his absence (while working in the USA from 2015 to 2017), the petitioner, in connivance with a bank manager, fraudulently opened an account in his name at IDBI Bank, Raipur, and deposited Rs. 1,00,000/-, leading to registration of FIR No. 170/2024 at P.S. Mujgahan, Raipur under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 34,
120-B IPC and subsequent filing of charge sheet.

However, the petitioner contends that the account opening formalities were jointly completed earlier with the complainant's consent, the amount was Shana Sonal Hoffman vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 2 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61565048/
1 deposited at his behest, and no transaction has taken place in the said account.

sentences.text:
It is further submitted that due to prior matrimonial discord, including allegations of cruelty, domestic violence proceedings, and a pending divorce petition filed by the complainant, the present complaint is false,
malicious, and filed with an ulterior motive to harass the petitioner and pressurize her.

Considering the submissions made by learned counsel for the petitioner, and in view of the fact that the dispute between the parties is purely a matrimonial dispute and a divorce case is also pending between the parties, as an interim measure it is ordered that till the next date of listing, the further proceeding of Criminal Case No. 89/2026 before the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class, Raipur under Section 120 (B), 420, 467, 468, 471, 34 of IPC shall remain stayed with respect to the petitioner.
Learned counsel for the Respondent No. 2 prays and is granted four weeks time to file his reply in the case.
Thereafter, learned counsel for the petitioner may file their rejoinder within two weeks.

Sd/- Sd/-
 (Ravindra Kumar Agrawal ) (Ramesh Sinha)
